label: Imposter syndrome
summary: Imposter syndrome in Maaike's work refers to the perceived knowledge gaps that conversation designers experience, the feeling of never knowing enough in a field that is still maturing. It shows up across all experience levels, not just beginners. It is one of the most commonly reported challenges in the Convoclub community, based on over 300 real answers.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike treats imposter syndrome as a practical problem to address rather than just acknowledge. She points to two concrete counters: finding or building a community of practice where people learn and support each other, and shifting into a growth mindset by asking reflective design questions instead of 'am I doing this right?' She also created a free course on handling your inner imposter inside Convoclub, and she is explicit that she experiences it herself.
open_questions: Does imposter syndrome in conversation design ease over time, or does the fast pace of the field mean it persists regardless of experience level?
How effective is a community of practice as a counter to imposter syndrome when the field itself still lacks solidified standards and tools?
